items.stem: Let $f(x)=2x^{2}-x$. What is the average rate of change of $f$ on the interval from $x=-2$ to $x=1$?
items.hint: The average rate of change on $[a,b]$ is $\dfrac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a}$; work out the two outputs separately first, and keep the brackets around the negative input.
worked: So the average rate of change is $-3$.

items.stem: Let $f$ be any function and let $h\ne 0$. Which statement is true?
items.hint: Write the average-rate-of-change formula with $a=x$ and $b=x+h$, then simplify only the denominator.
worked: The average rate of change of $f$ on $[a,b]$ is $\dfrac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a}$: outputs on top, inputs on the bottom.
Take $a=x$ and $b=x+h$. The bottom becomes $(x+h)-x=h$, and the top is $f(x+h)-f(x)$.
So the average rate of change on that interval is $\dfrac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h}$, which is exactly the difference quotient.

options.text: The difference quotient always reduces to $\dfrac{f(h)}{h}$, because $f(x+h)=f(x)+f(h)$.
The average rate of change of $f$ on the interval from $x$ to $x+h$ equals $\dfrac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h}$.
The difference quotient always reduces to $f$, because $f(x+h)$ means $f$ times $(x+h)$.
The average rate of change of $f$ on the interval from $a$ to $b$ equals $\dfrac{b-a}{f(b)-f(a)}$.
